data.name: Chop and Drop VR
data.detailed_description:
VR Chop and Drop is an experimental VIVE Serious Game that is free to play!

Take on the job of a line worker removing troublesome trees! Get out your chainsaw and use your control levers to maneuver the utility bucket in all directions, but watch your head!

When you reach a branch, get sawing! Each log dropped gives you points. Cut them safely and efficiently for the highest scores!

The game contains two modes, timed and freeplay. In timed play, you have 4 minutes to cut as many logs as you can. Enter your name on a local leaderboard when you finish! Or, you may use freeplay mode to take your time, explore the mechanics, and channel your inner lumberjack. Brought to you FREE by Designing Digitally, Inc.


Features
Cutting Physics - Pull the trigger to bite into a branch, and move the controller to complete the cut. Then, watch the log fall away. Be sure it doesn’t land on your head!

Timed and Freeplay Modes - Measure yourself against the time limit, or take your time sawing and chopping every branch and log into tiny bits!

Local Leaderboard - Compete with others for a high score or beat your own score within the allotted time.

Standing Only Needed - No room scale necessary. Stand inside the bucket and use the levers to move your space smoothly from tree to tree with a visually grounded platform. No teleporting!

It’s Free! - We are experimenting with virtual reality for Serious Games at Designing Digitally, Inc. and want to share a fun serious game we developed with the public.

reviews.review:
[h1]Played On: [b]HTC Vive[/b][/h1]

Chop and Drop puts you in the shoes of a powerline worker who has been tasked to remove some pesky trees before they take down the powerlines. The game offers two play modes: the regular game, which gives you an allotment of 4 minutes to perfectly remove 6 trees, and freeplay, where you can take your time removing said trees. You can make the utility bucket go in every direction, including up and down, and of course you'll be using a chainsaw to shred the trees to pieces. Each piece of the tree that is removed nets you points, but if you get any in your utility bucket, or if any pieces hit it at all, you receive a penalty to your earned points.

For a title that was released over a year since VR initially came on to the scene, Chop and Drop could be a lot better. By this point, most gamers have seen better and more immersive gameplay. The title doesn't bring anything new to the table, and its cumbersome need for players to have an incredibly long reach may mean some seated and standing gamers will either knock over items, bump their walls, or even hit their monitors. While it isn't awful, and it does perform well in the optimization department, there are a lot better VR games to experience.

[h1]Rating: [b]2.0/5.0[/b] - It's not awful, but it's not great.[/h1]

reviews.developer_response:
Indeed, there are better VR experiences out there with larger scopes. Chop and Drop was our first VR project and we wanted to share our own exploration into VR for others to try. We’re sorry you didn’t have the best experience
It is important to note about the reaching issue. People should always be careful using VR but this game does, in fact, require more than normal reaching if you cannot move the bucket into place. 
Again, sorry you did not have a better experience playing Chop and Drop but we appreciate your feedback and will keep that in mind for our upcoming developments.
